title: She'd lost her first Super Series final the year before. This time, she didn't let it slip. November 20, 2026.
excerpt: PV Sindhu's first Super Series Premier title, and a government assessment of India's PLI schemes that's honest about where the money landed and where the jobs didn't.
bodyHtml:
She'd lost her first Super Series final the year before. This time, she didn't let it slip

On November 20, 2016, PV Sindhu beat China's Sun Yu to win the China Open, her first Super Series Premier title, winning 21-11, 17-21, 21-11 in Fuzhou - the top tier of the BWF Super Series circuit at the time, and a bigger title than the Denmark Open final she'd lost the year before. Sindhu had already won Olympic silver at Rio 2016 just months earlier; the China Open title showed that result wasn't a one-off.

India's PLI schemes hit 76% of their investment target. Jobs are a different story

A new NITI Aayog assessment (with IIM Ahmedabad) of India's Production Linked Incentive schemes shows investment reaching Rs 2.4 lakh crore - 76% of the full-tenure target - and production/sales hitting Rs 22.6 lakh crore, 64% of target. Jobs are the weak link: the schemes have created 8.49 lakh jobs against a target of 30.2 lakh, just 28%. The report itself flags underperformers including bulk drugs exports, medical device employment, and IT hardware investment.

Two different kinds of follow-through today - one where the finish matched the ambition, and one where the government's own numbers say it hasn't yet.
